title: Delivery guarantees: at-least-once and the idempotency it forces

videos.script: Every stream in this course delivers each record at least once. At least once means sometimes twice. {{twice}} A producer sends a payment and the answer gets lost. It cannot know whether the payment was written, so it sends it again. Now there are two. {{retry}} A consumer adds a payment to a total and dies before it writes down how far it got. When it restarts, it adds that payment again. {{crash}} Nothing reports an error. The totals are simply wrong, and somebody sends them to finance. {{wrong}} In this lesson you will make that happen on purpose, with a consumer that crashes halfway and starts again. {{demo}} Then you will fix it. Each payment carries an order id, and a conditional write in DynamoDB refuses an id it has already seen. The totals come out right however many times the stream is replayed. {{fixed}} And you will see why exactly once is never a setting. It is something the whole pipeline earns, end to end. {{end}}
